raw_segments.text: Fragile in every sense of the word, they are obliged to look up to man for every comfort.
In the most trifling dangers they cling to their support with parasitical tenacity, piteously
demanding succor, and their natural protector extends his arm or lifts up his voice to guard
Perhaps the frown of an old cow or the jump of a mouse, a rat, would be a serious danger.
In the name of reason, and even common sense, what can save such beings from contempt,
even though they be soft and fair?
